item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight: Green Man's Chefs
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

They are extremely hostile to living things, especially humans except for their human employees.

This feels like a weird outlier in your pitch; like…why are the SCPs chefs cooking for humans when they hate living things and especially humans? It feels to me that this'd be more effective if they like were over friendly or whatever and just really wanted to please with their meals whilst also being alien and not really getting that like…cooking a human kills the human?

and no one has seen the restaurant's kitchen. The restaurant shut down due to sanitary reasons.

This feels a little incongruous to me: generally a restaurant being shut down for sanitary reasons would be like cos the food storage is disgusting or something; and so like…need access to the kitchen to know?

Tests were made with various non edible materials and the resulting dish is reported to be delicious no matter what the ingredients were and how it was prepared.

I'm not really sure that it's worth putting this in the article; it feels…like it might just be quite info-dumpy.

I think on the whole, this feels…like a really interesting idea that just needs you to do something interesting with it? Like I think part of me really just wants a like, investigation log where a foundation agent goes in and orders food and just, experiences gradually weirder and weirder things until they finally break into the kitchen and discover some shocking secret about it before the piece ends, y'know? Or just…some sense of the Foundation doing something with like the capture chefs or the investigation that's interesting and not a vague nod to how it was found or w/e.

item.title: Re: A Canary In The Coal Mine
item.content:encoded:
I didn't communicate it well, but Dr. Gables wants this researcher to get an SCP designation and he want whatever pay rise would come with it, so he wants the research data while expunging his own involvement in it.

Also him snapping was gonna be a build-up as the reader realises that this man has something weird going on. He would eventually reach the tipping point where he realises that he didnt consider if he got the cause and effect mixed up, aka. this researcher drinking a can of this soda wasn't a premonition but instead a trigger, and thus must be eliminated for 'the sake of humanity'.

The foundation, being a greyly moral organisation, can't deny the correlation and data even if it was collected in a way they wouldn't have done it in.

Do those details help clear it up? Or does the logic still seem weird? My only issue is why the foundation wouldn't lock up this researcher in case it is a trigger instead of a premonition. I though it might be funny to hand wave it away with a memo from the 'Department of Temporal Relativism' stating that 'In essence, they are both pretty much the same thing'

Thanks for the feedback!

item.title: Re: Greenlight request- Frozen Corpse and Nervous System
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

I guess I'll explain what I can about the narrative; I wasn't going to, since this is only a brief initial pitch, but hopefully you'll find this to be interesting at least.

If you want greenlights on an idea, you have to pitch the whole idea and not just some of it.

My concern with the narrative here is that it feels…lacking in closure? It might work if you can get a reader to feel invested in the SCP and so it being frozen indefinitely ends up feeling like a huge sad moment; but it feels like it might be hard to land that in a way that works? Particularly since the freezing here is implied to be perfect (i.e., that they've circumvented the usual issues where ice shards form within a body and rupture the cells); and so in turn, there's an implication that even if they wait a really long time, they could still wake her up?

The other issue with doing a sad ending here is that it feels like it might be really hard to get a reader to emphasise with the legs here; like…it's not like they can really talk and be a character and so you're likely going to have to rely on characterising them via their actions and mannerisms.


I'm willing to greenlight this though because I don't think either thing here is a major issue, and I think it'll be easier to tell if it works via a draft y'know? This said: there's a possibility this might work best as a tale and I'd urge you to seriously consider that. It'd allow you to spend a lot more time in the researchers mind if this was like…a write up of that investigation happening and his reaction to stuff, than if like, he has to formally write it up in a SCP file, y'know?

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight On My Idea
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

I have a multitude of ideas for these interviews which (as I haven't begun writing them yet) aren't super fleshed out, but have, what I think is, a good basis.

My concern with the ones you've listed out is that it feels like it's lacking a sense of coherence: they don't feel like they're building off each other so much as like, four completely separate interviews that could fit in any order.

I understand the "Native American curse" concept may be somewhat overdone

It is both really overdone and pretty problematic and I would urge you to not do this.

That said: the core story of the person here is the most interesting aspect of this to the point where I'd probably focus the story around like…what drove them to do this and how it gets wrapped and stuff; everything before this feels like a really lengthy preamble that doesn't add a tonne, y'know?

Everything after that in the log, will be mostly excluded/expunged, menial information (pH testing, and marking the times the fountains appear) as to avoid massive exposition.

I'd probably suggest not putting a tonne of menial information in this, or massive expunged sections: at the end of the day, you're wanting to write something interesting for a person to read and not a complete accounting on this.

An addendum will tie things up, from one of the interviewers, warning that further disruption of the phenomenon could be genocidal

This feels…overblown? Like, it's a relatively localised phenomenon and so it doesn't feel like this is a credible threat. But even if it did, having someone just kinda…say that this is the case feels like it'd be a really underwhelming way to show it?

I think my strongest advice is to focus this arc on the person who made it; and why they made it, and how like, the Foundations attempts to contain this/the person affect it's working. Like the angle of the foundation bringing him into containment and then the fountain killing a bunch of folk is interesting, particularly if we can kinda see the maker go through an arc where e.g. they realise they made a mistake here or something?

item.title: Re: Intergalactic blackmail
item.content:encoded:
Okay so I have two big concerns here. The first is that narratively, it feels like this is very similar to SCP-4645 in style; down to the like, random blackmail claims and the unclear like, requirement for what the foundation should do.

The second is that this doesn't really go anywhere: you introduce the mystery of who is sending this and that the blackmail changes repeatedly but it doesn't go anywhere. Like, the foundation doesn't investigate who sent it, they don't really debate whether to accede to the demands, they don't refuse and have progressively worse things happen; so it just feels very…flat?

My advice: figure out how you can show why this is interesting. Figure out what the narrative arc of this is.

item.content:encoded:
Deleted an article by Stolle 7B at -21 with three staff votes, standard deletion process.

Description: SCP-5392 is a humanoid creature resembling a young female adult approximately 3.06 meters tall with long arms stretching its entire body length and legs 0.96 meters tall. Despite being humanoid SCP-5392 shows no signs of human intelligence or speech, only mumbling unrecognizable language in raspy utterance. SCP-5392 has long, silky, black hair and its epidermis is completely gray in color. It wears a pale, torn, ragged dress, appearing to be a wedding dress. Its face is long and thin, with pale beady eyes and no nose. Its mouth is full of thin, jagged teeth, but has no tongue. The inside of SCP-5392 is completely epidermis, with no muscle, bone, or organs. Origins of this creature are still unknown.

No feedback present.

Deleted an article by Agent Dragnel at -19 with three staff votes, standard deletion process.

Description: SCP 5655 is an elderly male measuring 2.12 metres in height, SCP 5655 wears a red drizabone which has multiple toys and bells dating from the 1950’s attached to the exterior. All toys show signs of corrosion and rot. SCP 5655 has high levels of pigmentation and obesity. The hands of SCP 5655 are normally worn by mildly damaged Christmas mittens, SCP 5655 will only take these mittens off when aggressive. SCP 5655 hands suffer from severe frostbite and overgrown nails ranging 2-4 centimetres in length, it is unclear how the fingers of SCP-5655 remain attatched.

Feedback is as follows:

+ Karakatt
– Karakatt

Howdy hey

As stated before posting:

Remember: The main site is for summary judgment of final work, not feedback and critique on unfinished work.

It is your responsibility to post only finished, final work. Site members are not required to justify or explain their votes.

If you understand all of the above and still wish to create this page, click here to do so.

Readers are not required to review your articles since the site is for finished works only. It was your responsibility to receive critique by our IRC Chats or our idea critique forums.

+ Greenburger
– Greenburger

This one has a lot of issues, but lets start with the positive. I like the idea of a decomposed justice-loving Santa. But your execution leaves a lot to be desired.

Firstly, there are a couple of plot holes. There are probably millions of crimes committed in the month of December in just America alone. If this SCP showed up for every single one, the foundation would have a serious problem preventing the public from finding out about it. To fix this, perhaps you can change the article so that this scp only appears for extremely heinous crimes.

The same goes for instances where the scp shows up to give people presents. The scp showing up to give people presents could result in the public finding out about anomalies. The foundation needs a way to prevent the public from finding out, so either remove this bit or add a way for the scp foundation to track the scp so they can amnesticize individuals who were exposed.

The concepts also leaves a lot of unanswered questions. For instance, can the scp be in two places at once? If a bunch of people commit a crime at the same time but in different places, will the scp appear for only one person, or will a manifestation of the scp appear for all of the people.

Another question is if people have to "fix their unlawful act" for the scp to leave them alone, what counts as fixing an unlawful act. If you murdered someone, would you need to find a way to bring the person you murdered back to life. You need to create a specific set of rules that can be applied universally.

Additionally, you never specify what powers the scp has. Can it teleport? What if you try to fight it while the scp is trying to disembowel you. Does it have a way to immobilize its targets through combat or an afflicted paralysis? That needs to be specified.

Finally, why do people exposed to the scp need to be killed if any unlawful act can summon the scp? That seems excessive and inefficient, which is why the foundation wouldn't do it. It seems more likely that the foundation would investigate what those individuals did and determine and appropriate response. Additionally, why does the tree as well as the dishes/containers for the milk and cookies need to be incinerated. You said that was to prevent contamination, but I thought the scp only affected individuals who did unlawful acts. Is the scp diseased or something?

Overall, there are lots of unanswered questions and glaring plot holes.

There are also lots of issues with you grammar scattered throughout the article. I'm not going to list them all since this is already a long post, but one example is in the very first sentence, where you use "is" when you should use "are". There are several other mistakes like this throughout the article

You also have a bad habit of making your sentences to long by writing in a very indirect and convoluted way. For instance, you wrote:

"SCP 5655 will manifest nearby an individual who has committed an unlawful act in the duration of the month December."

The first issue is that you tend to use a conjugation of "is" before every verb in this sentence (manifest and commit). You should do that sparingly at most. It would be better like this:

"SCP 5655 manifests near individuals who commit unlawful acts in the duration of the month December."

Another way to cut down on fluff is at the very end of that sentence, where you wrote "in the duration of the month of December". "In the duration of" is just a long and convoluted way of saying during, so that can be shortened to "during the month of December", giving us the final edited version of that sentence:

"SCP 5655 manifests near individuals who commit unlawful acts during the month December."

Writing it like this is clearer and more concise. Most of your sentences have issues like this, which makes the overall article sound unprofessional. That takes away from the immersion of the entry, since the foundation is supposed to be all about cold professionalism.

Deleted an article by bruh my yeezys at -17 with three staff votes, standard deletion process.

Description: SCP-5645 is a humanoid superficially resembling an afro-latino male in late adulthood. It is outfitted with a ████ brand beige fedora and suit adorned with a laurel green tie. Although SCP-5645 possesses wireframe glasses, it is unknown if it suffers from Hyperopia. Its primary language is spanish.

+ Elunerazim
– Elunerazim

While posting multiple times is major no-no, I honestly think this is a not-bad SCP and I think there's a lot of potential. Fixed a typo for ya, too ;).

+1, but the multitude of posts will likely get it deleted.

+ Scorpion451
– Scorpion451

There are a number of problems here, but the primary one is that this is merely a description.

SCPs are speculative fiction stories presented in the form of archival documents. Some are vignettes that paint an evocative scene over the course of a few paragraphs, some are sweeping multiple act novellas with twisting plots, some tell their stories through the ways that they toy with the framing itself… but at its core, every SCP is a story. That is the point of an SCP.

+ Quicksilvers
– Quicksilvers

Very interesting idea, but there are a few logical plot holes.

These noises include memetic kill-words such as “Cekliption”, “Diffechindic”, “Humplionicaned”, etcetera.

Why would you specifically spell out memetic kill agents in a document? Even if its a LVL5 one like you stated, that could count as something very volatile and dangerous.

I feel like you could really expand upon this concept - why does this SCP display the Berryman-Langford agent specifically if the agent is so volatile and used for one of the Foundation's most buried secrets? Why is it spreading it around? Is it trying to inoculate people against SCP-001's safety protocols? Is it trying to use them to kill people? I really hope that this gets a rewrite because I love the concept and it has so much potential.

+ Mikaelious
– Mikaelious

An SCP-5645 escape is designated an AK-Class Omega-Cognitohazard Scenario. It is in the best interests for the foundation and humanity that this does not happen.

I feel like the latter sentence could be cut off or altered; surely the Foundation employees know that an apocalyptic event is something they should try to prevent.

Deleted an article by Misaka321 at -12 with three staff votes, standard deletion process.

Cypher is a new agent.

It is what it is, spirited young man takes over the mantle of his father, a Foundation agent who died long ago. Educated at home, Cypher joined the foundation — and after watching a Foundation promotional video, he felt a sense of meaning in his life. So like a dozen other newcomers, he trains, tests — and hopes one day to "save the world," as the promo puts it.

Feedback is as follows:

+ Asdfaslas
– Asdfaslas

There's definitely a lot to unpack here but for some reason the thing that I feel like it's most important to tell you? "Eight pairs of eyes" is actually 8 people. Not 4 people. I can't explain why that bothered me the most, but it did.

I'm not sure why you used weird open circles instead of periods a couple times, out of nowhere. I hope you look through the style guides because many many things should've been capitalized that weren't (Foundation, Chaos Insurgency, probably other stuff I've lost track of already) and most of all I hope someone a bit more useful can come by and give you more detailed advice than I just did, because I can tell that you really cared and really tried here and I'm just not cut out to really help much.

+ Vivarium
– Vivarium

I personally think the biggest problem with this article is the fact that you are telling a lot more then you're showing. I feel like there is a lot of potential in this concept, so I highly recomend you take this idea to the Idea Critique Forum, and seek Critique from other more experienced authors then myself. I hope you give this another shot.

This was fine. Competently executed, and an alright idea. However, the strings of my heart were distinctly un-tugged.

Part of it, I think, was the repetition between the interview logs (recalled in an intensely weird way for people who are prisoners being used as human guinea pigs) and the final documentation, neither providing, so far as I could glean, any additional information. There's also the, in my opinion, rather pointless addendum, which adds nothing to the story.

My main issue, though, is that struck me less as a wistful reminder of half-forgotten memories, and more as forced sentimentality. Maybe I've spent too long reading the comment sections for YouTube mixes with names like "I ' M S O A L O N E" and "N O S T A L G I C A T 2 A M"1 but my reaction to the memories was less "I will never get these moments back" and more "Oh, I have read this exact comment thirty times before."

I'm glad that this has been enjoyable for a lot of people, but I am not a fan. -1

Footnotes
1. Also, yes, this obviously pre-dates that whole genre of videos by several years, but I'm just trying to provide context my reaction.

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Page Layout (Optional): standard layout. Special Containment Procedures, description, discovery log and testing logs

Elevator Pitch:
basic idea is, there is a character that appears in video games and corrupts the game every time the player fails or loses a level/life. once corrupted enough, the character appears in the foreground and grabs the player through the screen. trapping them in the corrupted game.

Central Narrative:
The scp foundation finds this SCP by going to a POI's last known position. Who claimed to be part of GAW (gamers against weed). when they find his place one of the agents turns on a TV and is pulled into the game. When tested the game cartridge, it is found that any video game that comes within a 200-300 meter radius of the cartridge becomes infected and slowly turns into duplicate.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
this SCP is unique in the sense that people will fear dying, pausing or leaving a video incomplete. which many people do IRL, giving more spooks the people trapped inside will still be alive and suffering in a corrupt, horrific and incompatible game. only being able to communicate when some plays the game.

Additional Notes:
second try at an SCP. hope this idea is better.

item.title: Seeking Greenlight: Green Man's Chefs
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

  • Green Man's chefs are green faceless humanoids wearing a chef's attire.
  • They are sentient and are capable of speech despite without having a mouth.
  • They are extremely hostile to living things, especially humans except for their human employees.
  • They can cook anything with any substance, material, and etc. except for pure metals.
  • The non-chef employees are humans and are unaware that the chefs are anomalous.
  • The customers do not know of their existence.

Central Narrative: In 19XX, a restaurant named Green Man's Kitchen suddenly appeared in Alaska. Ever since it's appearance, sightings of faceless green chefs were reported. People that lived near the restaurant claimed that most of their possessions were stolen. Some people went missing. The restaurant had a constantly changing menu and it never showed what the ingredients were. The employees said that they've never seen the chefs and no one has seen the restaurant's kitchen. The restaurant shut down due to sanitary reasons. The restaurant was then destroyed by a wrecking ball.

Investigators found that the restaurant had used different materials as ingredients for their food. Some of the ingredients also included humans, clothes, animals, [Redacted]. The SCP Foundation only managed to capture only 6 of the chefs. It is studied that when one of them have gathered a main ingredient, a door appears and the chef enters. After 30 minutes, the chef comes out with food prepared with the ingredients it has gathered.

Tests were made with various non edible materials and the resulting dish is reported to be delicious no matter what the ingredients were and how it was prepared.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: These entities can cook anything and the tests that can be done with their ability. Figuring out how these entities came and formed a restaurant and what their origin may be.

Additional Notes: This is my first SCP. So, it might be messy or not good.

item.title: The Three Sided Coin
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article and Tales

Genre: Horror

Page Layout: Standard SCP layout, Wild West layout (think Aces and Eights style) for first tale.

Elevator Pitch

  • Its an anomalous coin that will reveal 3 different sides when flipped over. The 3rd side is anomalous.
  • When the coin lands on the 3rd side it transforms whoever flipped it into a monster.
  • In addition if someone keeps the coin for a long time it will alter their behavior, making them kinda crazy but in a fun way.

Central Narrative: The coins most interesting part isn't the monster but more so what it does to the people in possession of it. It makes them more exuberant, more fond of games and gambling, risk, chaos, but not necessarily evil. Its like the coin makes whoever is holding it chaotic neutral,
but they just happen to have a chaotic evil toy in their pocket, so they're dangerous. The tales will focused less on the coin itself but more on the people its effecting.

Hook: The characters. The concept can be used pretty easily to create stories. The idea that this coin is just floating around and anybody can have it allows people to come up with their own interpretation of how the coin might corrupt someone. Plus the monster is pretty badass too in my opinion.

Notes: I have a draft tale and a rudimentary scp article already written if anyone is interested is seeing them let me know.

Genre (Optional): Modern events

+ show block

Special Containment Procedures: A copy of the scp is kept on hard drive kept in safe.

Description: Video is antimemetic. Foundation wants to know what happened in the video because Epstein was already on their radar for potential ties to a redacted GOI. Research with dangerous z-class mnestics was recently authorized

Document #XXXX-01: letter of authorization

Document #XXXX-02: Report on research with z class mnestics sent to O5. Contains test log with dialogue. Reveals that Epstein was murdered.

Document #XXXX-03: Internal document from O5 council. They believe that it was MC&D. Now they want to use that info to the advantage of the foundation.

Elevator Pitch: The surveillance feed of Epstein's death is anti-memetic. The SCP foundation wants to uncover the mystery of what happened as well as why it was covered up.

Central Narrative: Starting with the Description, I'm going to build a sense of an imposing conspiracy regarding Epstein's death. I will do this by hinting that Epstein was already on the Foundation's radar for being tied to a redacted GOI. I'm going to then hype up the efficacy of z-class mnestics by having their usage require authorization from the O5 council. Using Z-class mnestics as a benchmark, I'm gonna emphasize how extremely anti-memetic the footage. However, the testing will ultimately pull through and reveal that Epstein was murdered. Finally, in a post climax reveal, an internal document from the O5 council will reveal who they bbelieve murdered Epstein, tying back to the redacted GOI from earlier: Marshall, Carter, and Dark Ltd.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP focuses on modern conspiracies that I imagine everyone on the SCP wiki are familiar with (and maybe even buy into).

Additional Notes: I know that writing an article about Epstein requires care. If I make things to political, I can drive out half of the readers. I also have to make sure remain respectful to his victims. I'm aware of that responsibility and I won't post an article unless I'm confident that I satisfy both of those benchmarks.

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight - Lavender
item.content:encoded:
Heyo Follow-up!

EXTRA SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: A collection of objects with anomalous, antidepressive effects. These objects are (but not limited to): manifestation of feelings described as "relaxation, peacefulness, etc.", diminished symptoms in subjects diagnosed with major depressive dissorder, etc. Objects interact with each other and are essential between themselves (For example: Access to XXXX-2 can only be done by interacting with XXXX-1, XXXX-3 is stored inside of XXXX-2 and any sample taken will disappear when
exiting XXXX-2)

While there is more context here, the concept still comes across a bit flat as there isn't much to get invested in. Currently the skip still just feels like an antidepressant, with no major purpose or reason to really exist.- why and how will these objects be important? why should I as the reader care about it?

The narrative:

Central Narrative: Discovered in a lab of an unknown GoI. Consists of an air freshener, a room that can only be accessed by smelling the content of the air freshener, and a lavender plant contained inside the room. The objects manifest anomalous anti-depressive and anti-memetic properties, since subjects exposed to any of the XXXX objects will manifest a general feeling of well-being; but they won't remember any initial exposition. Audiovisual data stored in a digital medium will experience total corruption and will be intelligible, however, textual and analogue data storage doesn't seem to be affected.

Currently this is closer to additional info on the skip than a narrative, there isn't anything that really expands on the setup or shows what happens during the story. How does the Foundation find everything out? (assuming characters are included) how are they affected? What is everything building up to? whats the conflict? whats the main focus or theme?

The story still feels relatively unfinished as there isn't much to go off other than the setup. I'm not sure what direction the story will take, or how all of this will fit into a narrative. (from what I can see here (and the sandbox)) the narrative looks like it will be mostly based around the effects, which alone won't be able to carry the article as they don't offer much to the audience without any purpose or context.

Hook:

Hook/Attention-Grabber: There's a fourth object which is only known to high clearance ranks. It's a virus that is presumably the cause of major depressive disorder and it's linked to the human subconscious since unknown times. Cannot be cured with any current means and it's symptoms can only be diminished with antidepressants. Also, one of the three initial objects has a very high value to the Foundation; it's a Thaumiel, and has a very high possibility to counterattack XXXX-4. Linked to SCP-5000 narrative (or at least I tried)

The '4th object' still isn't really present in the concept or narrative, I'm not sure why its important or what role it plays. Along with this, I wouldn't recommend having the object cause an incurable depression, in the context of this it just feels like its being used as an effect.

-Quick second note, the skip should be able to stand on its own without needing to rely on other articles. I would highly recommend writing this as its own story as cross-linking can be quite hard to pull off.

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight.

- Overall the skip doesn't seem to have much behind the effects, which makes it feel a bit close to a "thing that does a thing".- whats the skips in-universe reason for existing? whats its purpose? how will all of this fit into a narrative?

-Some general advice on building narratives: try to get an idea of the beginning and the end, if you know what direction the narrative will take, then (generally speaking) it'll be easier to create.

If you would like me to give any further feedback, don't hesitate to send a PM, and if your looking for additional critiques or different perspectives, then I would highly recommend the butterfly squad. :)

cheers,

RED
